content: The Abortion Care Guideline is a publication by the World Health Organization (WHO) in 2022, available in both electronic and print formats. The electronic version has the ISBN 978-92-4-003948-3, while the print version has the ISBN 978-92-4-003949-0. The content is distributed under a Creative Commons license, which allows users to copy, redistribute, and adapt the material for non-commercial purposes, provided proper citation is given. However, the use of the WHO logo is prohibited, and any adaptations of the work must be licensed under the same or an equivalent Creative Commons license. If a translation is created, it must include a disclaimer stating that the translation was not produced by WHO and that WHO is not responsible for its content or accuracy. The original English version remains the authoritative edition. The guideline includes a suggested citation format: Abortion care guideline. Geneva: World Health Organization; 2022. It also provides cataloging-in-publication data and information on rights, licensing, and third-party materials. Users are responsible for determining whether permission is required for reusing third-party materials, such as tables, figures, or images, and for obtaining such permissions. WHO disclaims liability for any claims arising from the infringement of third-party-owned components. The publication clarifies that the designations and presentation of material do not imply any opinion by WHO regarding the legal status of any country, territory, or area, nor the delimitation of its boundaries. Dotted and dashed lines on maps represent approximate borders that may not yet be fully agreed upon. The mention of specific companies or products does not imply endorsement or preference by WHO. Proprietary product names are distinguished by initial capital letters. WHO has taken all reasonable precautions to verify the information in the publication, but the material is distributed without warranty of any kind, either expressed or implied. The responsibility for interpreting and using the material lies with the reader, and WHO is not liable for any damages arising from its use. The guideline is organized into chapters and annexes, covering various aspects of abortion care, including clinical services, law and policy recommendations, service delivery, and best practices. Supplementary materials include evidence-to-decision frameworks and key international human rights standards on abortion. Acknowledgments are given to numerous individuals and organizations who contributed to the guideline's development, including members of the Guideline Development Group (GDG), Evidence and Recommendation Review Group (ERRG), and External Review Group (ERG). Contributions from human rights advisers, technical experts, and institutional collaborators are also recognized. Special thanks are extended to the Evidence Synthesis Teams for their systematic reviews using the GRADE methodology, as well as to the guideline methodologists and the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine for their work on monitoring and evaluation. The Economics of Abortion review team and the International Youth Alliance for Family Planning (IYAFP) are acknowledged for their contributions. Observers from United Nations agencies and individual reviewers from implementing organizations provided valuable feedback on the draft guidelines. WHO staff members from the Department of Sexual and Reproductive Health and Research (SRH) and the Prevention of Unsafe Abortion (PUA) Unit played key roles in managing the guideline development process. Writing and editing support was provided by a team of experts, and administrative and communications support was offered by WHO staff and external consultants. The guideline underwent review by the WHO Guidelines Review Committee (GRC) and the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR), with a focus on integrating a human rights-based approach. Funding for the guideline's development was provided by the HRP (the UNDP/UNFPA/UNICEF/WHO/World Bank Special Programme of Research, Development, and Research Training in Human Reproduction), which is executed by WHO. The guideline also includes a glossary of key terms and concepts to ensure mutual understanding and consistency throughout the document.
